paras: The killing of Pedro Aguilar near Laredo was the killing of a Mexican man by a crowd during a fight among Mexicans at a place reported as Fernando or Fernandez, near Laredo, in late July 1882. After another man, Pedro Gomez, was shot dead, Aguilar complained that he had not had fair play, and the crowd killed him too. The item circulated in northern papers only as a one-sentence wire brief within crime roundups.

Ten days before the wire item, San Antonio's Evening Light carried a dispatch reporting that at Benavides, Texas, seventy-five miles to the south on the Texas-Mexican railroad, a man named Pablo Aguilares had shot and killed Pedro Gomez in a quarrel over monte and fatally wounded another man. That dispatch said the shooter "was captured and chained to a post" and that "Great excitement prevails," and a Pennsylvania roundup repeated the shooting with the name "Pablo C. Aguitares." None of the later reports mentions Benavides, so the coverage does not show whether the two items describe the same affair.

According to a St. Louis "Texas special," a fight among Mexicans at Fernando, near Laredo, ended with Pedro Gomez shot dead. Versions printed in St. Paul and Hillsboro, Ohio, said Gomez was shot "by the crowd," while a later roundup said he was shot "by some one in the crowd." Aguilar then complained that he had not had fair play, and "the crowd killed him also." No participant in the crowd is named, and no report gives the site, the time of day, or the size of the crowd.
No report of an arrest, inquest or prosecution appears in the coverage.

The Wheeling Register printed the item on July 29, 1882, under the headline "Two Murders and a Lynching," paired with the reported lynching of the mulatto "Mexican Frank" in Oldham County, Texas. The St. Paul Daily Globe ran it on July 30 and again on July 31 in its "All Around the Globe" column, and the Highland Weekly News of Hillsboro, Ohio, set it among its "Later News" on August 2. A rewritten version headed "Murderous Deeds" appeared in Wisconsin, Minnesota and Dakota weeklies from August 2 to 3, dating the fight "on the 27th" and placing it "near Laredo, Mexico." No paper commented on the killing, and the Black-press collection does not reach back to 1882.

The victim's name was printed as Pedro Aguilar in Wheeling, Pablo Aguiltar in St. Paul, Pablo Aguilar in Hillsboro, and Pool Aguiltar or Pool Aguilar in the "Murderous Deeds" roundup. The place also varies, from Fernando or Fernandez near Laredo, Texas, in the earlier versions to "near Laredo, Mexico" in the later roundup.
